picks.title: Rivanna gets FDA clearance for BoneEnhance ultrasound software
picks.excerpt: FDA cleared Rivanna's BoneEnhance AI software module, which identifies bone and surrounding tissues and highlights them with color-coded overlays on 2D B-mode ultrasound images.
picks.rationale: A regulator decision: an FDA clearance for AI bone overlays on point-of-care ultrasound, which clinicians use for needle guidance. The tagged 10-07 AIRS Medical card was a different company, a different device and a different modality (MRI).

picks.title: AI-powered ECG assessments may improve heart transplant rejection warnings
picks.excerpt: Researchers said they plan on testing the AI model in additional patients at several transplant centers.
picks.rationale: A clinical study in a defined patient group: AI reads routine ECGs to flag heart transplant rejection, which could reduce reliance on invasive biopsies. The 30-day history has no transplant or ECG-rejection card. The excerpt is thin, so the enrichment pass should pull the cohort size and accuracy figures.

picks.title: AI flags heart failure patients at risk of functional decline
picks.excerpt: “Instead of asking only whether a patient will survive, we need to ask whether they will be able to maintain the life they value after discharge,” one researcher explained.
picks.rationale: A patient-centered prediction study: it predicts loss of function after a heart failure discharge, not only death, which changes what discharge planning targets. It is a different study and outcome from pick 2. This is the second Cardiovascular Business card, which is the outlet cap.

picks.title: Doximity adds UpToDate to Ask in push to become doctors’ go-to AI platform
picks.excerpt: Doximity inked a partnership with Wolters Kluwer Health to embed UpToDate's evidence-based clinical content directly within Doximity Ask, the company’s AI clinical decision support tool.
picks.rationale: A product release that reaches clinicians directly: Doximity's Ask clinical-decision-support assistant, which a large share of U.S. physicians already use, now answers from UpToDate's evidence base. That changes what sources a physician's AI answers are grounded in. The 10-09 Suki card was a different company's product launch on the same UpToDate API, so this is a separate deal and release, not a repeat.

picks.title: From simulation to pedagogy: multi-model and randomized evaluation of structured AI standardized patients - npj Digital Medicine

picks.rationale: A randomized evaluation of LLM-driven standardized patients for training clinicians in communication. It is open access, so the body is readable. The tagged 10-11 card was an RCT of LLM pre-consultation versus ophthalmology residents, which is a different study and use.

dedup.note: SWAP (post-fact-check): removed the AuntMinnie 'Biograph highlights cardiac AI CT study' pick. It was clinic self-promotion: every author is from Biograph, the clinic selling the screening; the study is an n=84 preprint without peer review; and the article is a press-release rewrite that misstates the preprint. Backfill: Doximity+UpToDate in Ask (Fierce Healthcare, 10-21). The earlier run had dropped it as the same story as the 10-09 Suki/UpToDate card. On re-review it is a different company, a different product and a separate partnership announcement. The only thing they share is the Wolters Kluwer UpToDate supplier, so it counts as new. It is not claimed by another section, Fierce Healthcare had no other pick, and it has no biosecurity content. Other candidates rejected in the swap: Optellum-RapidAI (vendor integration PR, and it would make a second AuntMinnie card); the FDA genAI docket cluster (MedCity AMA, MedCity Abramson, Radiology Business RSNA), which is comment letters and remarks on the consultation already published 10-23 with no new FDA decision; the JAMA OpenEvidence study and the STAT commentary on it (same as the 10-16 Becker's card); the JAMA Netw Open oversight commentary (same story as the 10-18 2026.39048 card); STAT AMIE takeaways and the Nature Medicine News & Views (AMIE running story or commentary); STAT AI sandboxes (running story from 10-15); Radiology Business adult-to-pediatric adaptation (same study as the 10-14 Nature BME card); npj C-TACT governance (framework perspective); all NEJM AI items (no readable body); and the Korean promo and roundtable items (KIMES roundtable, Weisen, Vuno, Gates Foundation), which report no clinical or regulatory change. Diversity: 4 outlets (AuntMinnie x1, Cardiovascular Business x2, Fierce Healthcare x1, npj Digital Medicine x1). No pathogen or biosecurity content. The npj pick has an empty og_image, so ax-media must source an in-article image.
